line:
A marriage can survive a true no. It cannot survive a no that was only a wound looking for a second body. Protection is the no that guards the bond, not the no that wins the evening.

line:
A parent who comes down to a child's height does not lose rank. Rank was the costume. The person remains. Dignity is the choice to be seen without requiring worship.

A family that can clap for its own is already rich. The eye is the first thief, and it can be the first blessing. The difference is whether the good is allowed to remain in the other hand.

Generosity is not the opposite of need. It is need that has remembered other mouths. The first portion, not the remainder, teaches the house what it is.

line:
Healing speech is not sweetness. Sweetness can be a lie. Healing speech is accuracy with mercy. It names the hurt and refuses the insult that wanted to ride along.

What is despised at home is despised twice, because home was the place it should have been safe to be plain. Appreciation is looking that did not turn away.

line:
A marriage that has lost a child, or a parent, or a future, needs presence more than explanation. Explanation is a way of leaving. Sitting is a way of staying.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. 汶 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 決 ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A marriage in despair does not need a speech about gratitude. It needs one true plan for tomorrow that both people can bear. Make the plan small enough to be kept.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 決 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Make one plan for tomorrow small enough that both of you can keep it.

z: 汽 ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
In a marriage, revenge is often petty and therefore easy to excuse. The small cut, repeated, is how love is replaced by a contest. Mercy is leaving one cut unanswered.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 汽 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Leave one cut unanswered today. Do not announce the leaving.

z: 汾 ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Accountability begins when you can say, the heat was mine. Wisdom begins when you can say, it had a better door. Compassion begins when the person you nearly burned is still in the room, and you stay.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. 汾 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Before the second loud sentence, step into the doorway, not toward the person. Let the heat guard the house from outside.

z: 沁 ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Self-reflection is the moment you notice you needed to win. Accountability is saying so before you are forced. The turn from pride to dignity is mostly this small honesty.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla. 沁 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Admit one small wrong without a speech about your intentions. Stop when the admission is complete.

z: 沂 ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings are assigned the same story and different gifts. Envy calls this injustice. Admiration calls it a house with more than one lamp. Both lamps belong on the table.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沂 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 沃 ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沃 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 沄 ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Hospitality is the oldest sociology of the lasting house. The stranger eats first. The family that cannot do this for a guest will eventually fail to do it for itself.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele. 沄 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 沅 ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla. 沅 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 沆 ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沆 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 沈 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沈 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Sit with a person who is not ready to speak. Let ten minutes pass without fixing them.

z: 沉 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. 沉 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Eat together once without retelling the wound. Let the meal be only a meal.

z: 沌 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla. 沌 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 沍 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沍 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 沐 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沐 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell the truth of the wrong once, to the person, and then do not serve it at breakfast.

z: 沒 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele. 沒 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 沓 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla. 沓 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 沔 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沔 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 沕 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沕 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Name the person you are afraid of losing, and spend the next hour near them without a speech.

z: 沖 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele. 沖 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 沗 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla. 沗 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 沘 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沘 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 沙 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沙 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to perform a talk.

z: 沚 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele. 沚 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 沛 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla. 沛 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 沜 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沜 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it.

z: 没 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 没 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 沢 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele. 沢 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 沪 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. 沪 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 沫 ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沫 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 沭 ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ihlombe, ilunga, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu. 沭 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 沮 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沮 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

z: 沱 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele. 沱 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: If you gave someone a cruel name, retire it today, out loud, and do not use it again.

z: 河 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. 河 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Look at one ordinary object they mended or prepared, and say what it cost them.

z: 沸 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沸 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

z: 油 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 油 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: If you were the one who broke trust, say what you did without a speech about why it was almost fair.

z: 沺 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. 沺 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 治 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla. 治 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 沼 ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 沼 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell the truth of the wrong once, to the person, and then do not serve it at breakfast.

z: 沽 ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 沽 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: If you have already burned someone you love, say so before the day ends, and then do one ordinary kindness with your hands.

z: 沾 ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele. 沾 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

z: 沿 ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Across generations, envy of the young is fear of being finished. Admiration of the young is how an elder stays in the story without owning it.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla. 沿 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Ask the person to show you how they did the thing. Be a student for ten minutes.

z: 況 ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder who has been afraid and stayed is a better teacher than an elder who claims never to have shaken. The shaking, survived, is the lesson.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. 況 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Hold the doorway. Let the frightened one see that you are not leaving.

z: 泂 ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
An elder who gives the best piece away is not being careless with the future. The elder is showing the future how a house continues.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. 泂 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 泄 ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
An elder's stories are a kind of speech that builds or bends a family. Tell the story in which people are repaired. The other story will tell itself.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele. 泄 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Tell one story tonight in which a person in this house is repaired, not mocked.

z: 泅 ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder who still notices the small faithfulness in the house is a gift to the young. The young become what is noticed.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Here the body speaks by ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla. 泅 does not replace it. The character stands aside, the way a true name stands beside a person and does not erase the face.
practice: Ask to be shown a skill you had decided was beneath you. Watch the whole way through.

z: 泆 ingqe, indololwane, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
An elder's quiet can be a shelter or a locked door. The young can tell which, by whether they are welcome to come and say nothing beside you.

line:
A child believes the sentence more than the apology that follows it. Speak as if the sentence will live in them, because it will. This is not fear. It is care.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, ilunga lenqulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 洫 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Say the hard thing to the face, once, cleanly, with no audience.

z: 洮 ingqe, ilunga lenqulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The ordinary work, the meal, the repaired hinge, the repeated story, is the curriculum of a family. Thank the labor, not the performance of being easy to live with.

practice: Remove the sneer from a sentence and speak it again. Notice how much of it was only the sneer.

z: 洯 ingqe, ilunga lenqulu, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
A child does not need a conversation performed. A child needs a person who can be found. Being findable is the practice. The words can come later, or not.

line:
Forgiveness does not require the betrayed to be foolish. It requires them to decide whether the person is still a member. Membership is a practice after it has been a wound.

practice: Eat together once without retelling the wound. Let the meal be only a meal.

z: 洲 ingqe, ilunga lenqulu, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
A marriage that has lost a child, or a parent, or a future, needs presence more than explanation. Explanation is a way of leaving. Sitting is a way of staying.

practice: Answer the ordinary request of a grieving child. Do not make them perform a sadness you recognize.

z: 洳 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A marriage in despair does not need a speech about gratitude. It needs one true plan for tomorrow that both people can bear. Make the plan small enough to be kept.

practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 洴 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
In a marriage, revenge is often petty and therefore easy to excuse. The small cut, repeated, is how love is replaced by a contest. Mercy is leaving one cut unanswered.

z: 洵 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Accountability begins when you can say, the heat was mine. Wisdom begins when you can say, it had a better door. Compassion begins when the person you nearly burned is still in the room, and you stay.

practice: Teach the strong child to stand in front of the smaller one. That is anger, turned, and it can be learned young.

z: 洶 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Self-reflection is the moment you notice you needed to win. Accountability is saying so before you are forced. The turn from pride to dignity is mostly this small honesty.

practice: Praise a person in the house for a quality you do not share. Do not add a correction.

z: 洸 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Siblings are assigned the same story and different gifts. Envy calls this injustice. Admiration calls it a house with more than one lamp. Both lamps belong on the table.

practice: When a sibling is praised, add one true sentence of your own. Do not balance it with your own news.

z: 洹 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many houses, under many names, give the same command: do not be ruled by dread, and do not despise the person who is. The strong are asked to stay, not to sneer.

practice: Name the person you are afraid of losing, and spend the next hour near them without a speech.

z: 洼 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Hospitality is the oldest sociology of the lasting house. The stranger eats first. The family that cannot do this for a guest will eventually fail to do it for itself.

practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

z: 洽 ingqe, iqakala, phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Siblings remember the name they were called on the worst day. Do not give them that name. Give them the name of the good you have actually seen them do.

z: 派 ingqe, iqakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
Children who are met with contempt learn to hide the clumsy part, which is most of them. Appreciation gives that part a chair.

line:
The old practice of sitting with the sick, of keeping watch, of not filling the air, is this turn. Do not rush to be useful. Be there.

z: 浅 ingqe, iqakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
The wisdom shared by many houses is hard: do not let the sun go down on a break you are willing to heal, and do not call it healing if you are only waiting to retell it.

practice: Name the break once, without extra charges. Then do one small trustworthy thing, and repeat it tomorrow.

z: 浘 ingqe, iqakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Children grieve in strange hours and then ask for ordinary things. Both are grief. Answer the ordinary thing. Do not make them perform a sadness you can recognize.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, ngaphezu komaphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 浘 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Do not hurry a grieving person into cheer. Let the absent name be said.

z: 浙 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
A child who sees an adult look again, after a bad day, learns that a bad day is not a verdict. This is worth more than any optimism you could announce.

practice: Open the curtain before you decide what the day is. Let the house see you do it.

z: 浚 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Children are the usual casualties of a score kept between adults. They did not agree to carry it. Mercy toward the person you resent is also protection of the child.

practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 浛 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Siblings fight because they share a roof and a hunger. The fight is not the failure. The failure is when the stronger one discovers a liking for the smaller one's fear. Protection refuses that discovery.

practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 浜 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi phezulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Brothers and sisters are the first public. What you do to be admired at home becomes the way they will treat their own children. Give them a dignity they can copy.

practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 浞 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu
line:
The teachings that endured all warn the eye. They also bless the eye that rejoices. Rejoicing is not a mood. It is a decision made again each time the other person shines.

practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.

z: 浠 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Fear of the future makes a house small. Courage does not enlarge the future. It keeps today's people inside the house while the future remains unknown.

practice: Tell the truth you have been saving, and remain in the room after it is told.

z: 浣 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
Psychology is simple here. The closed hand teaches the body that the world is about to run out. The open hand teaches it that tomorrow includes other people.

practice: Put one thing you were keeping back into the middle of the table.

line:
Gossip is how a house talks about its own when they have left the room. Healing speech waits until they are back, and then says the hard thing to the face, cleanly.

practice: If you gave someone a cruel name, retire it today, out loud, and do not use it again.

line:
Across the old writings, the warning against scoffing is constant. A scoffer cannot be taught, and a house that scoffs cannot learn itself.

line:
Some truths are not ready for speech. Presence holds them without using them as a weapon. A weaponized silence is still a weapon.

practice: If your quiet has been a punishment, break it with one gentle sentence and then stay.

line:
A child who watches a break become a lifelong trial learns that love is a court. A child who watches a break become a mended bowl learns that love can survive its own failure.

z: 浪 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
Compassion is grief that has recognized itself in another body and does not hurry it. Hurry is fear. The unhurried hour is the gift.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 浪 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.

line:
The sciences of a lasting household call this resilience. The older word is faithfulness. It does not deny the dark. It refuses to let the dark be the only speaker.

practice: Decline the word forever. Keep the true sentence about the pain, and stop before the lie.

z: 浮 ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Many sacred traditions, in different grammars, say the same hard thing: the injury stops when someone declines to pass it on. This is not weakness. It is the end of a chain.

z: 浯 ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla
line:
At the table, anger wants the last word. The last word is rarely food. Let the sentence end before it becomes the story the children will tell about this house.

practice: If you have already burned someone you love, say so before the day ends, and then do one ordinary kindness with your hands.

z: 浰 ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
The guest at the table is a test you did not schedule. If your worth requires the guest to be less clever, less beautiful, less faithful, your worth is a costume. Take it off.

practice: Kneel, or sit, so your eyes meet a child's. Stay there until the conversation is theirs.

line:
What you wish were yours, name it exactly, in the hearing of the person who has it. Then do not reach. The naming is the confession. The not-reaching is the turn.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 浴 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.

z: 浸 ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele
line:
Name the loss you are counting. Often it is a person in the room, not a disaster outside. Then put your body beside that person. That is the whole practice.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokunxele. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 浸 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.

z: 浹 ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
Give before you calculate whether you will be thanked. Thanks are not the food. If you require them, you have made a trade, and a trade is not yet a family.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 浹 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.
practice: Give a thing away that you still like. Do not wait until you are tired of it.

line:
Wisdom is not silence forever. There is a time to speak. The test is whether the words can be repeated in front of the person, and still be a kindness.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, ngezansi kakhulu, ngakwesokudla kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 涀 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.

z: 涁 ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu
line:
Look at the work you have stopped seeing. Name it. The naming is not flattery. It is the return of sight, and sight is the turn.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. The member drawn is ingqe, iqakala, maphakathi eduze, kakhulu. Treat it as a member of the house, not as a specimen. 涁 is the seal, not the subject. The subject is the living relation.

line:
Put the glowing thing in another room. Sit where you can be seen. You do not have to be interesting. You do have to be in the house.

practice: Be findable. Tell the house which room you will be in, and be in it.

line:
Accountability is the first half. Without it, forgiveness is a fog. The one who broke the trust says what was done, without a speech about why it was almost justified.

practice: Decide, and say, whether the person is still a member. Do not leave them in a fog.

line:
The oldest writings are full of lament, not because lament is holy by itself, but because love that cannot lament becomes hard. Let the house be soft enough to cry.

practice: Leave the empty place unspoken-of only if the grieving person wishes it. Otherwise, speak the name.

line:
Despair often tells the truth about pain and then adds a lie about forever. Keep the truth. Decline the forever. Forever is not a fact available to a person at a window.

practice: Set one place at the table that despair said was pointless. Eat there.

line:
Accountability remains. Mercy is not the cancellation of truth. It is the decision that truth will not be used as a knife at breakfast for the next twenty years.

practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

line:
An elder who has turned anger into protection does not become mild. The wall is still warm. What changes is the face it turns toward. It faces the street, not the cradle.

z: 涍 isidiski phakathi kwamathambo, phezulu, ngakwesokudla
line:
An elder's dignity is not the right to be obeyed in every small thing. It is the right to be respected while still listening. The listening is what makes the respect true.

Envy is love of a good thing, twisted until the good thing must shrink. The love was real. That is why it hurts. Turned, the same look becomes admiration, which is fed by another person's light.

line:

Children learn what strength is from the body that stands between them and the weather. If that body spends itself on them, they learn that love arrives as weather. Turn the heat toward the actual danger.

A marriage becomes a grievance when the store is private. What is earned may be stewarded. What is hoarded becomes a wall between two people who share a bed.

line:
Do one undeserved kindness to the person you are keeping score against. Do not mention the score. The mention would turn the kindness back into a move.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Look long enough at i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 溧 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Do one undeserved kindness where you are keeping score. Do not mention the score.

z: 溪 i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele
line:
The counsel that lasted did not flatter rage. It asked the strong to become a wall for the weak. That is the ethic of a parent and of an elder: your size is a shelter, or it is a threat.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Look long enough at i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokunxele and the lesson stops being abstract. 溪 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: When the heat rises, name who you are actually keeping safe. Put your body between the danger and the child. Do not spend the heat on the child.

z: 溫 i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla
line:
The old wisdom is severe on the high seat. It is not severe on the upright spine. Stand up. Then let the others stand. A house of one standing person is a court, not a family.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Look long enough at i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla and the lesson stops being abstract. 溫 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Once, take the lower seat on purpose. Let someone in the house finish a story you could have told better.

z: 溯 i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu
line:
A child who is envied by a parent carries a weight no child can name. Admiration from above is a kind of safety. It says, your becoming does not threaten my place.

This is the work of the one who left and the one who remained. Look long enough at i-osteon, maphakathi, ngakwesokudla kakhulu and the lesson stops being abstract. 溯 waits at the edge. The work of the house happens in the limbs, not in the motto.
practice: Clap, or thank, before you comment. Let the first sound from you be glad.
